summary: AegisTS cleans multivariate time series with two hierarchical RL policies: a high-level one orders the quality issues (duplicates, missing values, outliers, constraint violations) and a low-level one picks a cleaning operator for each. A dual-stage reward couples cleaning quality and downstream task performance. 'Agent' here means an RL policy, not an LLM agent.

claims.claim: Up to 96% improvement in data cleaning quality
claims.evidence: §6.2: 96.4% NMSE reduction vs EDITOR on ETTh1 only. On IDF_OilTemp, Clean4TSDB has lower NMSE, and on Handwriting EDITOR has higher RRA/F1, so 'up to' is the best case on one dataset.

claims.claim: Up to 27% improvement in downstream performance; best downstream on all scenarios
claims.evidence: §6.2 downstream paragraph and Table 4 report the highest ΔPerf on each configuration (e.g. +0.1666 IDF_OilTemp). Single runs, no variance.

claims.claim: Works without ground truth or domain rules
claims.evidence: Evaluation still uses synthetically injected corruptions on clean datasets (following MTSClean) to obtain dirty-clean pairs, so the real-world no-ground-truth case is not tested directly.

patterns.note: Hierarchical high-/low-level RL policy; not an LLM planner-executor.

methodology.sample: 4 public datasets (ETTh1, IDF_OilTemp, Libras, Handwriting), 6 dataset-task configurations, synthetic corruption injection
methodology.baselines: EDITOR, Clean4TSDB, DiffPrep (adapted; single-series only), random sampling

standards.peer_review: None stated (ACM template placeholder text left in the front matter)

biases.detail: The 96% headline is the single best dataset/metric pair.
Corruptions are synthetic injections, not naturally dirty data.
No seeds or CIs for an RL method.

coi.affiliations: Zhejiang University, National University of Singapore, University of Fribourg, Aalborg University

verdict_reason: off-topic: RL-based time-series data cleaning. 'Agentic' refers to RL policies, not LLM coding agents. The headline numbers are best cases on synthetic corruptions with no variance and no code.
applicability: Not applicable. The team ingests healthcare education content (documents and media metadata), not sensor time series, and the paper has no bearing on agent harnesses, multi-repo coordination, agent hosts, or spec-driven development.
